utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, you are to continue with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, and thank you. Mr. President, Your Honours, given your decision yesterday with respect to the composite exhibits, I briefly need to go back to the 35-page exhibit to tender two pages from that composite exhibit, because at the time I understood that they were admitted. It will take me a couple of seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Please do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. The 65 ter number is 2465, and if I'm correct, I am referring to pages 6, 7, 8 and 9. If they can be brought up, that would be great.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness 138.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see a document on the right-hand part of the screen there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What is that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an expert report pursuant to a request to conduct an expert analysis following an impact of a projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we please move now to the last page, and that is page 9 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, do you see a stamp on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it in the lower right-hand corner. I can see the stamp there. This is a valid stamp used to certify documents of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see the name Emir Turkusic on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he carried out an analysis of all the physical evidence that was brought in from the site, and he signed here in the lower left-hand corner. And there's also the signature of his chief, who, in effect, certified this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does this document appear to you to be an authentic document from the CSB in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the kinds of documents produced there. This is the report following an expert analysis. I would see documents of this kind, but I did not see this specific document because it wasn't shown to me after the analysis had been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. President, Your Honours, I would like to offer these into evidence, these particular four pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, they are admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P130, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness 138, before I move on, I just want to briefly ask you one question with respect to the first incident we were talking about yesterday; that is, at Geteova number 12. Do you remember discussing that incident yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you were on site doing your investigation, did you notice any combat activity or military activity at that location at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no combat activity there or military activity. The only incident was the explosion, and this is a civilian neighbourhood. These are apartment buildings, private homes, and there were no military facilities there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'd like to bring up Exhibit -- it's part of Exhibit 185, and that is -- for the benefit of Mr. President and Your Honours, that is the composite exhibit related to the TV tower incident. And I am asking to bring up the sketch, the introduction to the sketch, and they are pages - for the benefit of the court deputy - 20, 21, and 22 of the exhibit. And might we go into private session very briefly, with your leave, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we could move to page 4 of -- the fourth page of this set of photographs, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, did you take these two photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took those photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Please explain to the Trial Chamber what these photographs are of.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph that we're look at now depicting the damage caused by the explosion of the projectile. This is the eastern wall of studio C, and the explosion occurred at the lower section of the wall, creating a large crater in the ground and damaging the foundations of the wall itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And this one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is, once again, the photograph of the damage but close up. You can see marking -- a piece of evidence marked with number 1. I can't recall what it was, but you can see in the key what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say "key," you mean on the sketch; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see all the damage itself on the black part here. You can see something that is marked with number 1, and then below the photograph there is some text, and there you should have the explanation of what it was that I actually marked with this number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you see that explanation now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Number 1 is used to mark the damage to the wall to help me know what was what.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could the court usher -- sorry, court deputy please move to page 6 of this exhibit, and if we could move to the lower photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see an arrow on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I put the arrow in there. It shows the damage to the wall facing the studio C wall, the eastern wall of the studio C.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say "damage to the wall -- to the eastern wall of studio C" -- sorry. "the damage ... facing the studio C wall," how was that damage caused?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photograph you can see quite a lot of damage. You can see that all the glass was broken and that windows were punched out, but this damage is different. You can see here a burn mark, which indicated to us that this was probably caused -- in fact, it was caused by a projectile hitting this wall causing this damage and then bouncing off to land finally next to the wall of the studio C. All the other damage, you cannot find the burn marks next to them, which means that the rocket actually caused this burn mark on this wall as it hit against it. And the rest of the damage was caused after the explosion itself. It was caused by the fragments of concrete, iron and steel, and all the other objects that were flying in all directions after the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So in terms of the sequence that you spoke about yesterday, this mark on this wall comes after the projectile bounced off the roof and before it exploded; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the trajectory of the projectile itself, the first point of impact of the building was on the roof; we saw that on the sketch and on the photographs. It continued along its path, hitting this wall, ricochetted off again, and bounced off back at the wall of the studio C, and then it exploded right there at the bottom of the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask the witness, how is he in a position to tell us about the trajectory, the movement, of this projectile, that it bounced from one wall to the next? I mean, what is the basis of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we arrived at the site as a team, as I said, there was an investigative magistrate and an expert who carried out an expert analysis of the fragments of this projectile. A great deal of physical damage was caused, and the inner courtyard had high walls. And we couldn't really figure out how it actually managed to fall in, so we did investigate this matter. We climbed up on the roof and we found this first impact site, and then we concluded that the projectile ricochetted and then we followed the direction of the -- possible direction of the projectile, and that led us to the -- this mark on the wall. It tallied with the direction that we concluded was one of the possible directions, and then we concluded that this was the only possible explanation for the actual trajectory of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You referred several times to "we," "we did this." Who constitutes "we"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not the only one to determine the trajectory. The entire investigating team, headed by the investigative magistrate, the inspectors from the security services centre, from the Novi Grad police station, the expert for this kind of projectile who provided his report, we all came to the conclusion that this was what actually occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You had an expert for this kind of projectile who was part of the investigating team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he did give us his report. I don't know whether he really was an expert. I'm not in a position to judge that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, is that -- are we going to hear from that person?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: We are, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: We are, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are. Okay, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, just following on from Mr. President's question to you, how did you establish that the impact on the roof was related to the explosion in the atrium? How was it established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The television building was not targeted by shells in those days, and there had been no marks on this building previously. When we inspected, when I inspected this mark, it was fresh. The gravel and all those things, they were freshly disturbed. And if a mark is old, you can really determine that quite easily. You can see dust on it. Because of the peculiar climate in Sarajevo, dust settles fairly easy. We have dust, we have fog and things like that, so this was definitely a fresh mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say "a fresh mark," just to be clear, which mark are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the roof itself, it was covered first with some kind of a tar board. It was all broken up, and then there was gravel on top of it. It is very easy to determine -- when you see a stone that has been broken, it is easy to determine whether this was done recently or whether some time had elapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So you're talking about the mark on the roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'd now like to just go through the photographs very quickly and for the witness to identify that they were his photographs, and then tender them into evidence. So we would start from this page and go to the end, and that is to page 36.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, did you take these photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took those photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to offer these set of photographs into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, they are admitted. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we saw the bodies of victims. Can the Prosecutor please explain to us, is this pertaining to the RTV building incident, since we have not heard yet that there had been any casualties in this incident. All of a sudden we see photographs that seem to have nothing to do with the event that we've been dealing with over the past two days, and it has not been stated at all whether these victims are, in fact, related to this incident at this site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, lay the foundation for these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I was going to get to them. If we could move to the -- perhaps they can be removed from the screen for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, were there any casualties in this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one person was killed in the explosion of this projectile, as far as I know. I received this information after collecting all the physical evidence, and then we went to photograph the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you personally photograph the body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did photograph the place where the body fell down when this person died and the place where this person was taken to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we go to -- very quickly to page 8 of the photographs, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we were supposed to hear by now when this person -- where this person was killed. We've been discussing this incident for two days, and we have yet to hear where this person was killed. I don't know whether it's a he or a she. And that's -- we cannot really discuss this unless we know it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Had you finished with your intention to lay the foundation for the photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have heard that the witness took some photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you took some photographs of the place where the person was killed, is that right, in this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the page in my photo file with the photographs that I took. Number 3 marks the spot where the body was found. The staircase inside the inner courtyard leading to the main building of the radio-television, and the lower photograph is yet another photograph of the body itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, is this a photograph of the site where this person was killed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I mean, those are questions that you might find it proper to ask in your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the Prosecutor should explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, actually, I was just going to ask for this sketch to be put on the ELMO so that Witness 138 can show the place on the ELMO where the person was killed. Perhaps we can just clear the screen of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, can you just, first of all, with your pointer, point to the place where the person was killed in this incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say for sure that this is where he was called [as interpreted]. Blood-stain was found there. This is the staircase leading from the atrium to the main building. It is possible, though, that he was here, that he was pushed away by the blast, and that he started bleeding there. But we did find blood-stain somewhere midway down the staircase, and we marked this place with number 3. So this is the blood of the victim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is that where you found the victim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When we arrived, the victim was taken inside the building and photographed. In the photograph that we saw a minute ago, traces of blood were found, a puddle of blood was found, and I marked it with 3, and that's what it says in the legend attached to the sketch of the scene. According to eye-witnesses, the body was taken from the staircase to the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How did you -- how was it established that this person was, indeed, killed from this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the only body recovered or found inside the building. Upon our arrival to the scene, the colleagues who were in charge of information and interviews with witnesses acquired this information. And also on the basis of the evidence found on the spot, the blood on the stairs, et cetera, we established that this person had been killed at this exact location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you please mark where you pointed to, to where you found the blood by the staircase. Can you just mark that with the letters BS in red. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P132, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, was there only one person who died, or were there other casualties but you only made one photograph of this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my knowledge, there was one victim and I photographed this victim. It is possible, though, that in other cases that I dealt with, that there were other casualties; however, in this particular incident, there was only one casualty. I am not -- I was not authorised to interview witnesses, which was shown later in the reports compiled by other members of my investigating team pertaining to the casualties, their personal details, et cetera. And all of this constitutes a whole file pertaining to this particular case. The only information that I had at that moment I inserted into my file, including the photographs, et cetera; however, it is possible that in their official report there are some supplementary information that they had acquired from people in hospital who had been wounded, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we please move back to the photographs and go to page 10 of the photographs. I'll try and be brief because the pictures aren't particularly nice to view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see those photographs on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I took these photos and they're an integral part of my photo file.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps we can remove the photographs now so I can ask a question without it being on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, is there anything you can say with respect to the marks on the back on those photographs -- well, how do the marks on the back of the victim correspond to the explosion at the wall at studio C? Is there anything that you can say about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: An interesting thing, when we examined this body, we noticed a multitude of wounds all over the backside of the body, from his feet all up to his head, and before that we had never had a body with this kind of marks. It is probably stated in the post mortem report that this was caused by fragments of the concrete that dispersed and hit this person in his back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are a few more photographs -- I mean, I can take the witness through them, but at this stage I would like to offer this set into evidence, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P133, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May we now, again, go to Exhibit 185, and to pages 528. And, Mr. President, could we please, with your leave, move into private session very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And could the court deputy bring up pages 13 to 16 of the same exhibit, 185. Thank you. And for the benefit of the Court, the translation ERN is 00683940 onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said a while ago, I'm making tremendous effort from the very beginning, with the help of all my spectacles, but I can't read anything else apart from the signature. If we don't have this enlarged, it is completely useless. Then it would have been much better if we could have hard copies in our hands, because with my spectacles I'm unable to read this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It has been enlarged, I think. No? In English, yes, but in B/C/S ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It has been enlarged in the English text, and I believe the B/C/S is a little clearer now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just slightly, believe me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we must be thankful for small mercies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: All right. Witness 138, do you see that document on the right-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document. That's another report drafted by a colleague of mine following the event in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What kind of report is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an expert report of the evidence collected with regard to an explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if we could very quickly move to page 16, that is, the last page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, do you see a stamp on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the -- I can't see it now. A moment ago it was in the right-hand corner. There was a name and a stamp, and in the left-hand side corner there's a signature. To the right is a signature of the head of the department, and to the left is the signature of the person who conducted the examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does that stamp appear to be -- appear to you to be an official stamp from the CSB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's an official stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And does this document appear to you to be an authentic document from the CSB in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This kind of reports and expert reports looked like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I offer that document, pages 13 to 16, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P135, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, lastly with respect to documents in this incident, I have a series of stills that were taken from the DVD, 360-degree photograph, which I would like to present to the witness, and I have copies for Your Honours and counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a photograph there on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What is that a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an aerial photograph of the TV building, and you can see this section where the incident in question took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you point to the -- to the place of the first impact on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the place of the first impact, which we explained when we discussed the sketch. It has been sketched and photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could you please take your pen and mark at that place -- mark on that place the letters FI.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, with a straight line, can you follow the direction of the projectile into the atrium from that point, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And can you just please tell the Trial Chamber, the second -- the left-hand set of circles that you see on the left, does that indicate where the atrium or the courtyard is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This right-hand side circles is the roof of studio C, and the left one that I'm showing now signifies the atrium where the projectile landed and exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'd like to offer that still into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P136, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness 138, when you were investigating that incident, did you at any time notice any military activity there or in the vicinity of the TV building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice any military activity inside the building or around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you see any ABiH mortars or tanks or military hardware in the building or in and around the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, after this incident, did you investigate -- did you go to investigate another incident on that day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel. Before we leave this incident - and I understand from your question to the witness that we're moving on to the next incident - but before we leave the TV incident, could I please ask you to ask the witness if the direction of the projectile, as the witness showed to the Chamber, where -- if that is in any way revealing the place from which the bomb was shot. What is north and what is south on this picture? And if this is the incoming direction of the bomb or the projectile, then where was the projectile shot from?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour, I will ask that question. Perhaps the still could be put back on the ELMO for that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, in your on-site investigation, did you -- you and the team determine the direction of fire of the projectile on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only thing that we did was to determine from which direction it had come. That wasn't part of my remit. Probably it had been established afterwards wherefrom it had been fired. We just established the place of the explosion, the direction from which it had come, and other pieces of evidence surrounding the event itself. But we didn't establish the source of the fire. It came from the west, but from which particular location I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I was just going to ask the witness if he could indicate north and south and east and west on the map -- on the photo, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]. [Interpretation] So S indicates north, which is down here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's at the bottom, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe a few degrees to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, is that clear enough? I could ask the witness to mark the direction in -- with the English letters. No? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If he's able to, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, before you mark anything, could I -- please mark the direction north with the letter N, if you haven't done so already.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And then please, just for completeness, continue with west -- W for west --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: -- south and east, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Does the witness have any idea whether the Serb troops were at that time placed at any particular position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Sarajevo was surrounded from all sides and I know that on the west side as well they were there, but I don't know precisely where their positions were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the ABiH forces, do you know whether they would have been placed at any particular position at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably the BH forces were in this -- within this same ring, because otherwise they would have been broken through into the town, and therefore I presume that the Bosnian army had set up their ring around the town as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prosecutor, can I ask you to ask the witness to identify the TV building on one of the maps that you have provided the Chamber with, because we would like to see where the incident took place in geographical terms in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, Your Honour. What I had intended to do, because there were quite a few incidents within a particular area, which I thought at the end of my examination of these incidents, I would ask the witness to mark en masse the positions that we've discussed in the examination on a map, and for it to be tendered in one go, so to speak. But I can do it in another fashion if it's more agreeable to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's up to you, but it will facilitate the Chamber's understanding if at one point we are offered the locations in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Absolutely. I was intending to do that. Might I just inquire, I would like to have the recently marked still, with your leave, Mr. President, admitted into evidence as a separate exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted. [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand this has already been admitted, so we'll keep it as the same number -- or will you wish it to be marked separately?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I was just under the understanding that with the markings of north, south, east, and west, it had not been admitted at that point. But since they were added, I think it would be preferable to have it as a separate exhibit, if it's convenient for the court deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let's have it as a separate exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours and counsel, this is one document, one physical document, and I can't split it. What I can do is assign a new exhibit number. The old exhibit number was P136. The new exhibit number would be P137, and P136 would just not exist any longer, if that's preferable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Court Deputy. [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The exhibit will be 136, with the marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So, Witness 138, after the investigation into the TV incident, did you conduct another investigation on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After this incident we went to the Geteova Street where there was a building, an apartment building, at number 5. This had also been struck by a modified air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you remember, approximately, what time did you get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember this, but it is contained in the official report. But I do know that in terms of the time-line, I first did an on-site investigation at the TV building and then went to do the on-site investigation there at this other location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Who did you go -- who did you go there with for that investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was accompanied by an investigative magistrate and part of the team that had conducted the investigation at the TV building. But I do think that a part of the team remained at the TV building because there were quite a few inspectors from the security services centre and an expert who went on searching for the fragments and investigating the explosion, whereas we had to do the on-site investigation at the Geteova Street location. The names of those who took part in the investigation at number 5 Geteova Street are contained in the official report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: For this investigation did you complete an on-site investigation report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did a forensic report. I did the photo file on the basis of the photographs that I had taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could the court deputy bring up 65 ter 767, and it's pages 18 and 19. And, Mr. President, could we please move into private session, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just very briefly describe what this photograph depicts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an area in front of an apartment building. You can see Alipasino Polje. This is part of Alipasino Polje called "B faza." This is a road passing by the apartment buildings. This is an asphalt road. And these are all the traces that are left there after the projectile hit the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see the top photograph there on the screen, Witness 138?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see this photograph. I took this photograph. It depicts the damage to the northern side of the building caused by this explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And this apartment block is on the street, Geteova number 5; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's number 5 Geteova Street. That was the road that was covered in debris that we could see on the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down to the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is this a photograph of the same building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same as the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May we move to the next page, please. You can just keep both of them on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Again, Witness 138, just briefly describe these two photographs and tell the Trial Chamber if you took them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took both of the photographs, and they are all part of my photo file. On the upper photograph you can see damage caused by the explosion of the projectile, and the lower photograph depicts the entrance to the building, the access route to the building, and all the debris, the rubble, that fell down in this area after the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Counsel, could you please ask the witness if he could indicate on this last picture - if you could turn to what we had just before - to indicate, if he can, the direction -- the entry direction of the modified air bomb into this building, if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, from the top photograph, are you able to indicate the direction of entry of the projectile; and if you are --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I will mark with an arrow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arrow marks the point where the projectile entered the building. It is difficult to indicate the direction from which the projectile had come from. It is difficult to mark it on this photograph. Perhaps I should have just marked the spot with an X.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is that because you are uncertain about the direction from which the projectile came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Because of the angle from which this photograph was taken, the place where I was when the photograph was taken actually causes these problems. It was not -- this photograph was taken right in front of the location; otherwise, I would have been able to show you the direction. When I am shown the map in front of me, I will be able to show you that, because then you can see the position of this building and then I will be able to show you the direction from which the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before you do that, can you tell me what experience or knowledge do you have that would enable you to give that kind of information. By that I mean the direction from which the projectile came. Do you have any experience or knowledge in projectiles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, on the basis of the physical evidence I found at the scene - and I know this building because I had been to buildings like that many times before and I know where the staircase is located - the supports of the projectile were found here, because they got embedded into the building. You can see here the large-scale destruction. Three floors were destroyed. It is difficult to say this on the basis of this photograph, but we as a team that got there, and on the basis of all the evidence we were able to find in the building, we were able to determine the direction. But my colleagues had eye-witnesses who confirmed -- the eye-witness reports confirmed this because they had seen the projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's the team -- that's the team which includes an expert in projectiles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But I have to wonder whether you have enough experience or expertise in this area to give valuable evidence on these matters. But let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps we can have this photograph admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of the answers which he gave, we wouldn't admit this because he has said that he is unable to identify the direction on the photograph, although he thinks he could on a map. So perhaps you could put a map to him. And also because he has said he doesn't have any specific expertise in this area. So we won't admit this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I'll just move through the rest of the photographs just so the witness can authenticate that they were his photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, did you take these two photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took this -- these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the last page. Thank you -- the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take these two photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the same for these two, did you take these two photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, in this incident --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we just hold the photographs for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you establish whether there were any casualties in this incident, Witness 138?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were casualties. At first I received the report that two persons had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said: "At first I received the report that two persons had been killed." Did you receive different information after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In my report I put things that I learned at the site, and then through later inquiries conducted by my colleagues, I did not learn anything about any possible further casualties, people who were killed or wounded. And I remember just one name of one person who was a casualty in this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take photographs of the casualties in this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did. The photo file should contain those photographs. I can't remember now, but if there are photographs in this photo file, then I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next one and keep it on the frame very, very quickly, and then for the next one as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, did you take those photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And did you take those photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, could we have the photo file admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P139, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Under seal, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, I got mixed up in the numbers. I think we jumped directly from P136 to 138. Could you please check if that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are at the time for the break. Mr. Sachdeva, two hours had been estimated for this witness, and so for you've had three hours and 40 minutes. I am to say that the underestimation will not affect the time allocated to the Prosecution to present its case. We're adjourned for 20 minutes. The Chambers will be consulting on some matters during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Sachdeva. The Chamber apologises for the late start. We had to carry out some consultations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Could I start with having exhibit, which is the map, 2878 brought up onto e-court, please. Is it possible for this to be enlarged a little bit. Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, is that a map of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a map of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, are you able to point out where the TV, the radio-television, building is on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, here's how I want you to do it: First take the pointer and mark to it -- just point to it at the moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Would it help if he simply -- if Witness 138 simply identifies it with a pen. If it's proving difficult right now, I can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Could we have Exhibit 767 -- sorry, 65 ter number 767, page 17 of that 65 ter number brought up, please. For the benefit of the Court, the English translation is ET 00375008.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, do you -- do you see a B/C/S document on your screen there, Witness 138?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is that document, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an official report of the inspector from the security services centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And does this report pertain to the incident at Geteova number 5 on the 28th of June, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It's a document drafted by this official and it pertains to this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does this document appear to you to be an authentic document from the CSB in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the heading, you can see the name of the official employed in this institution, and you can see his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'd like to offer that into evidence, that is, page 17, I understand, of Exhibit -- of 65 ter number 767.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P140, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the next exhibit, might we move into private session, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If the court deputy could bring up pages 23 through to 27 of 65 ter 767.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, same questions for this document. Do you see a document on your screen at the moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the document. This document that I can see is one of the documents relating to this case. It has been compiled by a CSB inspector. I can't see his name at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just for the Trial Chamber, the English translation is 0037 -- sorry, ET 00375014 to 00375018. Could we have the B/C/S version up on the screen, please. That's page 23 of the exhibit -- of the 65 ter number 767. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an expert's findings who examined the evidence collected at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if we could quickly move to page 27 on the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a stamp on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, on the right-hand side of the document, including the name and the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And is that an official stamp of the Ministry of the Interior or the CSB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's an official stamp of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And does this document appear to you to be an authentic document from the CSB in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, I'd offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit Number P142, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness 138, after you investigated the -- this incident, the one we've just spoken about at Geteova number 5, did you also conduct another investigation on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the incident at number 5 Geteova Street, we went to Safeta Hadzica Street where also a projectile had exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Whereabouts in Safeta Hadzica Street did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The explosion took place in the area around the heating plant. There was a boiler-house -- boiler-house and the so-called Kuwaiti infirmary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What was the Kuwaiti infirmary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an out-patient clinic for civilians, for the patients living in this civilian area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the heating plant that you just said a moment ago, was that a military or a civilian installation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was a civilian facility. That was a plant that had been -- existed there from before, and they served for providing heating of this neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you said that a projectile had exploded at Safeta Hadzica Street. I want to ask you: How did you come to know about this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the Novi Grad police station. This is where my headquarters was. And the explosion happened in the vicinity of the police station; or, in other words, the police station itself was at the center surrounded by all these three locations of explosions that I investigated on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you said that you were at the Novi Grad police station, why is that significant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this period my department was in the building of the security services, and in order to reduce the risk of travelling to and from the work or walking around the town, a certain number of people were relocated to police stations. I was living in this area and it was more convenient for me to go there and work on the cases that happened in that particular neighbourhood. Some of my colleagues were transferred to other police stations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, this incident is at Safeta Hadzica Street?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's -- do you have the number of the house? The reason I'm asking is that in the Chamber's ruling under 73 bis, we excluded evidence being led on incident number 16 of the 28th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, this -- the number of the street is 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Forty-four?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is this a pharmacy?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's excluded. We excluded it, so no evidence is to be led on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, with your leave, might I make a submission on that point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, it's not open to you. We have already decided that evidence was not to be led on this incident, under Rule 73 bis. What would your submission be?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: My submission would be that it -- would be this: That from the invitation of the Trial Chamber, we put forward a proposal to drop a certain -- a few incidents in terms of proving them beyond a reasonable doubt in detail, as with the other scheduled incidents. However, the Prosecution did indicate clearly that we would lead evidence of these incidents in a more general nature, so as to assist in proving the campaign, the general campaign, and the widespread and systematic nature of the campaign of shelling and sniping. And with Your Honours' order and decision wherein it had granted -- it granted the Prosecution motion in full, it was the Prosecution's understanding that such evidence could be led in a more general fashion, so as to prove widespread and systematic nature and the general campaign. That would be my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is this related to the submission that the Prosecution made about leading evidence on unscheduled [Realtime transcript read in error "scheduled"] incidents? Is this the same thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Actually, it does tie in to that, because of course to prove a campaign we have, indeed, a -- specific incidents appended to the indictment; however, they are simply illustrative incidents. And we also intend to prove unscheduled incidents. And so, in our submission, while we have been prohibited in leading detailed evidence on these incidents, the Prosecution submits that the incident has, in a sense, been transferred to the category of unscheduled incidents. And in terms of notice ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead. I had my mike on and I've been chided about that, so I was turning it off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Thank you. What I was going to say is, with respect to notice, and that is before this witness was to testify, of course the procedure is that the Prosecution discloses to the Defence the exhibits that we intend to use, and of course the exhibits pertaining to this incident were included in that list. And, of course, this incident is on the present 65 ter summary of this witness; and as such, the Prosecution is of the -- it's the Prosecution's submission that the Defence does, indeed, have ample notice of this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think it's not a question of notice. Just let me say that the transcript doesn't have my question correctly -- what I asked was whether this was related to the submission that the Prosecution made about leading evidence on unscheduled incidents. I'll consider your submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is good that this issue has been raised at this particular moment. Yes. What my learned colleague is saying, yes, all of this has been disclosed; however, the way these things have been dealt with in these days is within the human powers. However, everything else exceeds the limits of human capability of any team. Why am I saying this? In a few days you're going to rule on a witness that is supposed to come and testify here in a similar fashion as Mr. Witness of today, and it's up to you to decide. The testimony of this witness, yes, it is true we did receive 23 binders, and for this witness we have been allocated one hour. Once this witness arrives, I will be compelled to bring all these 27 binders for you to see and judge whether it is impossible for me and my team to deal with this. But this exceeds my powers, and this witness is identical to the one currently being questioned. Under such circumstances, we absolutely believe that it's impossible to achieve or to get minimum conditions for fair proceedings. We can dispute or try to dispute every single incident, and it's up to you to rule the incidents that are contained in these binders in a less-convincing way than it was the case so far, in our view. After our submission, we expect that you are going to rule very soon, but this witness is scheduled to testify next week. So, quite simply, this is beyond human capability and normal proceedings. And I appreciate your raising this issue because very soon you'll be facing this problem. Only one hour has been allocated for this witness, and the documents relating to this witness are -- contain about 10.000 pages, just to say the least. So we're all going to find ourselves in a situation that we're going to have a witness and hundreds and hundreds of incidents and thousands and thousands of pages relating to his testimony, and this is the result of very fierce fighting rather than the intention to kill people in a most reckless way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tapuskovic. Anything in reply before I give the ruling?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm unaware of the witness learned counsel is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not dealing with that. I'm dealing with the question that you raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I'm being given another opportunity to say something, all I would say is that we have been -- I can see counsel is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this witness has already been announced. I can give you his name, his full name. He's not a protected witness. His name is Cerimagic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, we are dealing with a submission made by the Prosecutor. When we come to that issue, we'll deal with it. I invited you to speak on that issue, not on something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, what I was about to say is that, as Mr. President and Your Honours are aware, we have been, and we intend to lead evidence of a more general nature from other unscheduled incidents, and this incident has, in the Prosecution's submission, been transferred to that category, and it would -- it would, in the Prosecution's submission, would be illogical for us to not be allowed to lead evidence of a more general nature of this incident. And I would also add that this incident is one where we do not allege that there were casualties, firstly; secondly, it's a short and compact incident and it essentially will take 5 to 10 minutes of examination time. And those are my submissions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, the Chamber is not with you on this issue. In our view, your analysis is not correct. Under Rule 73 bis, the Chamber has a discretion to identify a number of crime sites or incidents in respect of which evidence is not to be led by the Prosecution. In exercise of that discretion, the Chamber did identify those sites and this incident is one of those. An unscheduled incident cannot be, by definition, an incident in respect of which the Chamber has expressly exercised its discretion and decided that evidence should not be led in relation to it. An unscheduled incident is an incident other than one of those incidents that the Chamber has identified as an incident in respect of which evidence should not be led. I note that paragraph (F) of Rule 73 bis does allow the Prosecutor to file a motion to vary the Trial Chamber's decision as to the number of crime sites or incidents in respect of which evidence may be presented, so that was a facility open to the Prosecution, but that has not been exercised. In the circumstances, the Chamber will maintain the ruling that it made when it exercised its discretion under 73 bis (D) and will not allow evidence to be led on this particular incident. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Then I shall move on to another incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, you had just started to talk about an incident at Safeta Hadzica Street on the 28th of June. Now, what I want to ask you is: Did you investigate another incident at that location during the summer months of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did investigate another incident, a shelling incident, at that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Are you able to tell the Trial Chamber exactly where on Safeta Hadzica Street that incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a shelling of this very neighbourhood itself. There are several streets there Majdanska, Safeta Hadzica, and Prvomajska, the 1st of May Street, and this the area bordered by those streets was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you recall when that incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was on the 26th of May, 1995, but it is in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell the Trial Chamber what happened in that incident on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that area, from the police station where I was down to the Majdanska Street, several shells fell and so did a modified air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And how were you informed of this incident, and how did you -- well, how were you informed of this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, I was in the police station, the Novi Grad police station, and I heard the explosions of the shells. And then later on the shift leader, who was on the ground floor, told us where the shells had impacted and where this projectile had exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you know where exactly the shell had impacted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to the site later on and I did photograph the entire site, and the site of the explosion of the modified projectile which had hit a roof of the apartment building at number 52 Majdanska Street, destroying several apartments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you produce a report from your on-site investigation that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did a forensic report and I photographed the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just going back very briefly to what you said earlier. A moment ago you said: "Several shells fell and so did a modified air bomb." With respect to the several shells, can you give any more description about these shells?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say that when those shells exploded, or rather, when they hit, some exploded and some did not. I know that we inspected the area we found an unexploded shell and we also found a shell that had bounced off the asphalt area, hitting a house that was located there; it did not explode. It simply broke apart because of the force of the impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Was there anything in particular with respect to the markings of these shells that you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that on this unexploded shell there was an interesting thing. There were some numbers there. There were some Nazi symbols there, the swastika and some other symbols, Nazi symbols, in effect; they were carved into the shell. It looked as if it was, in fact, engraved by a machine into the shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you recall if there were any casualties from this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that there were casualties, but I can't recall their names and their number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to offer -- to show the witness a document and ask your leave to move into private session for this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, do you recognise this photograph and did you take it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took this photograph. This is a close-up of the explosion site that we could see on the previous photograph, marked with an arrow on the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the sixth page, please. Sorry, I think it's the one before that. That would be -- just the photograph before this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the location on this apartment building where the projectile struck. This is what it says underneath the photograph, the location on the apartment building Safeta Hadzica Street, number 102, between the third and the fourth floor where the third projectile hit. When I say "the third projectile," it is not -- we do not know the sequence of the projectiles, but this is the sequence in which we investigated the impact sites of those projectiles. So we went first to the first one, the second one, the third one -- that's the third one that we investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you know what kind of projectile this is or this was caused from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were shots fired from cannon -- shells fired from cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the third-last page of this exhibit -- 65 ter number. That's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see that photograph on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the photograph. I took this photograph, and it depicts the entrance to number 52 in Safeta Hadzica Street, where a projectile -- a modified projectile hit and exploded on the fifth floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Are you able to see the marks of the explosion on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the ground floor of this building, this is the entrance to the building, so you cannot see any marks of the -- made by the explosion of this modified projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, what does this -- what does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph depicts a part of the apartment -- the fifth floor apartment that was destroyed. Since this is the last -- the top floor of this building, you can see the damage, no walls, no roof, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what was this damage caused by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The damage to this building was caused by an explosion of a modified projectile. The photograph that we saw a little while ago where the shell exploded or hit between the third and the fourth floor, the damage is much less, which means that the modified projectiles have a much higher destructive power.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we now move to -- I actually want the -- I want to tender these photographs into evidence, this series of photographs; however, I suspect I would have to show the witness each one of them, and I can do that if need be. Can we move to the second page of 65 ter number 766, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And this one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what was this damage caused by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph that I've just seen depicts a car that was hit by a shell that exploded on impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And is this photograph on the screen a picture of the same car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's another photograph of the same car.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we could move to -- not to the next page but the page after that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 4 marks the crater caused by the projectile in the yard of Dzemaludin Causevic elementary school -- I'm sorry, Musovic. The letters here are quite small.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, same question for this photograph: Did you take it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took this photograph, and there's an explanation stating that this is a crater caused in the asphalt playground of the Dzemaludin Musovic elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this event is not among the scheduled incidents. We don't have it. Which incident in the indictment does this refer to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, what incident is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: This incident is incident 10 on the -- in the amended indictment, that's Safeta Hadzica Street, number 52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: 26th of May, 1995. We charged -- we charged a modified air bomb explosion, but in this series of photographs there were, as the witness has been saying, other shells that landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but this is a school that we're talking about. The school is not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, eureka, I found it. It's very much there. And I expect you also have it. You haven't looked well enough, or perhaps you're still having trouble with your eyeglasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I don't. But a school is mentioned here and no school is mentioned in the indictment; that is why I got up. No school is mentioned here in the indictment, whereas schools -- the school was mentioned in the testimony. And I've had -- I have had problems with my eyeglasses all my life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the mere fact that he mentioned a school and the school is not mentioned in the indictment wouldn't exclude the evidence being led if the evidence substantially relates to the incident in the indictment in other terms. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Can we move to the next picture, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And in this photograph, the sixth projectile that we investigated fell in the area between the elementary school and the building on number 102 Safeta Hadzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, did you take this photograph; and if you did, please explain what it is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This is an unexploded projectile that landed behind the building on 70 Safeta Hadzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you find this projectile on the day that you were doing the investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. It was found on the same day, and this number 7 indicates the seventh location that we reached in the order of our investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we could jump two pages and go to the one after that, so the third page from here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, did you take this photograph; and if you did, what is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took this photograph. And one can see in it a projectile marked number 8, or the eighth location in the sequence of our investigation. After hitting the house, it did not explode; it only disintegrated due to the power of impact. This yellow powder marked 0 is an explosive charge from this shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if we could move to the last one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph, and what is it, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This photograph shows a part of the projectile found on the fifth floor, or number 52 of the same street, and it's marked number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And where does this projectile -- what kind of projectile is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- this is a part of this modified projectile, and I think this is a rocket carrier -- there is an expert witness findings and report, because the expert was sent to investigate and examine what kind of projectile was in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I believe there's one more page. Very well. Mr. President, I'd offer these photographs into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P144, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could we now bring up Exhibit 13 -- 65 ter number 139 and pages 5, 6, 7 from that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, do you see a document there on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is that document, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an official report, or rather, expert's findings, an official finding of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And which incident does this report pertain to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It pertains to the report that we had seen previously on the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we go to page 7 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, the same questions. Do you see a stamp on that document -- on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
