utterances.text: Yes, I do. I see the stamp, the signature of the person who certified this, and also the name and the signature of the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just to be clear, is that an official stamp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's an official stamp used to certify this type of document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does this document appear to you to be an authentic document from the CSB in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'd offer that into evidence, that is, pages 5, 6, 7 of 65 ter number 139.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber admits it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P145, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I have a hard copy of the map that I was trying to work on beforehand. Could that be placed on the ELMO. I've been told that the e-court map is working, and perhaps we can try it that way first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let's try the e-court map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That would be 2872, 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, let's try again. Is that a map of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I'm looking at the map of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Are you able on that map to, first of all, indicate where the TV building is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps it could be zoomed up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And maybe it can be moved towards the -- I think it's left, to show the left-hand side of the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So, Witness 138, please mark by the TV building the letters TV.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, from -- are you able to see the roof of the building where the first impact occurred? If not, that's fine. But if you are, please just put the figure -- sorry, the letter R right beside it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's impossible in this kind of map. It's approximately somewhere where the upper line of the T letter is. But in this type of map, it's not very easy, and I wouldn't like to be -- to make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. Are you able to draw a line in the direction from where the projectile came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Please, on top of the arrow, just place the letter P.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, just to be clear, how did you establish the direction of fire, namely, from where that arrow indicates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the physical evidence that I already explained, this arrow indicates that it was coming from this direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was it the witness who established the direction from which the projectile came or the team with which he was working?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you hear my question? Was it you who established the direction from which the projectile came or the team of which you were a part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The whole team established that. But at this particular instance it was very clear, because there were two marks that the projectile left; therefore, it would have been able for me myself to establish where it had come from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it your evidence, then, that in some cases you are able, independently of the team, to establish the direction from which a projectile might have come, but in other cases you are not so able?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said is that based on certain marks that the projectile leaves, it is possible to establish the direction where it comes from. I -- for that I need two bench-marks, and I did have them in this particular instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But suppose you didn't have those bench-marks to guide you, would you have been able to do it independently of the team in another instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It depends on the type of explosion. When you have a mortar shell exploding, based on the traces that it leaves, it's impossible to detect the source of the shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It is possible to detect the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: From what you said, I gather that there are some instances when you would need the team, as a whole, to identify the direction from which a projectile might have come. Can you give me an example of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The judge was conducting the investigation and he set up the team. It wasn't me who did that. So based on the traces of explosion, if it happens that we had an explosion like the one on 52 Safeta Hadzica Street, when the projectile hit the western side of the building, it was very simple to determine where it had come from. Even in the case -- in case of an unexploded projectile, you have ricochet and you have these two marks, so it's simple to determine. If you have only one mark, like with mortar shells but also -- but based on its traces, it is possible to determine the incoming direction. When you have an explosion of a modified projectile, as was the case on number 5 Geteova Street, the projectile was embedded in the western side of the building and damaged it. However, there was no damage on the eastern side of the building; therefore, it is very easy to say that it had come from that particular side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't believe you have understood the question that I asked. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, I just want to clarify one thing that you said in response to Mr. President's questions. When you talk about mortars, are you able to determine the direction of fire, as opposed to the firing position or the origin of fire? What are you able to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only determine the direction of the incoming projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, Witness 138, just please clarify for us, you have told the Trial Chamber that on some occasions you are able to determine the direction -- the direction of fire of a projectile and in some cases you are not, and the team assists in that regard. Can you give an example of those cases where you yourself are unable to determine the direction of fire of a projectile.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't my duty to establish exactly the angle in topographic maps; however, I can determine the direction. I cannot say exactly whether it has come from the west or what, but there was always a person there with a compass determining the angle and the number of degrees of the angle of the incoming direction. But based on the traces I was able to determine the direction. For example, let me tell you about number 5 Geteova Street. A portion of the building on the west side exploded; therefore, nothing happened on the east side or the southern side of the building. Based on the projectile embedded in this building, one can clearly see that it had come from the west. And whenever I had two points or two bench-marks on the basis of which I claimed it came from the west, another member of the team, working with a compass, established the exact direction. But based on the traces it was possible to determine whether it came from the west, from the east, from the south, or from the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And in respect to the TV building, did you have those bench-marks from where you were able to determine approximately the direction of fire of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, the exact place of explosion. And we had a marker on the roof which indicated the first place of touch. That was the first bench-mark. And the second bench-mark was the place of impact. So we had these two bench-marks, one where the projectile ricochetted and the second one where it landed. So we could have, based on these two, established the incoming direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, how did the -- as you put it, the first place of touch on the roof of the TV building enable you - and I'm talking about you yourself - to determine the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the place of explosion itself. If we look at the TV building now, the explosion took place to the right from the touch point between the modified projectile and the building. It ricochetted and it went down to the eastern wall of studio C, and this is where it exploded. If we had found any marks on the other side of the building - and we didn't - one could have assumed that it came either from the north or the west. However, according to the damage that we detected, we could establish the direction, the incoming direction, of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the marks on the roof, were you able to establish anything from the marks on the roof with respect to direction of fire? That's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon inspection of the damage to the roof, as I just explained, there was a tar layer on the roof and a layer of gravel and this tar roof was twisted in the direction of the incoming projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. I want to move back to the map. The map is still on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you now, for the benefit of the Court, mark the place where you conducted an on-site investigation on the 22nd of June, 1995, at Geteova number 12, I think it is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's number 12 Geteova Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you above the cross just place the letter G and the figure 12, as small as possible, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you do the same for the incident at Geteova number 5, on the 28th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you mark the place at Safeta Hadzica Street where the incident occurred on the 26th of May, 1995, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This place is here on the map bordered by Prvomajska Street, now called Majdanska. At the time this was all Safeta Hadzica Street, and this is this area here. You can see the school here and the police station as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you, to the right-hand of that cross that you just put, place the letters SH, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, do you know where the military barracks, Viktor Bubanj barracks, are located; and if you do, if you can mark that on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be here. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: To the right of that cross, can you please but the letters VB.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, in the area where you've marked the two incidents on Geteova Street and the one on Safeta Hadzica Street, were there any other military facilities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no military facilities. That was a residential area, apartment buildings and office buildings that had all been there since before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Was there a -- was there an office that soldiers used to use in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were some offices there used intermittently by uniformed soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And how large were these offices, roughly, in square metres, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am familiar with the offices because I pass by often. These are offices maybe 50 or 60 square metres in surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And are you able to tell the Court how many soldiers would typically be in those offices?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite frankly, I don't know. I'd see uniformed people there, but what they had there, how many people were there, bearing in mind that this was an area of about 50 to 60 square metres, I really didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you mark on the map where those offices were with the letter -- with the figure O, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to offer this still into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, could you ask the witness also to, just for clarification, identify on the map where the police headquarters were, where the victim -- the witness, sorry, was present when some of the shellings happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, you've told us that you were occasionally in your police station in Novi Grad. Can you mark that also on the map with the letter P -- actually, not P because there's already a P there. PS, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is located here between G12 and SH, and it will be a little bit difficult for me to write this down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does that clarify it for Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I offer this still into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. And it's time for the break, but let us hear the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become P146.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're adjourned for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, we must be concluding this examination-in-chief. You have to consider whether the level of detail is necessary for the case that you are presenting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I intend to finish shortly. Before I start again, has the map been admitted into evidence? Might it be removed, please, from the screen? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, I just am now going to ask you very briefly some questions about another incident that you investigated. Do you remember an incident involving a bus that you investigated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember investigating an incident involving a bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when was that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall the exact date, but I do remember this investigation. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you know the year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in 1995, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, just explain very briefly what was the incident that you investigated. What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- in fact, I did do this bus -- one bus incident. It was an Elektroprenos bus that was moving towards Dobrinja, and it was hit at the intersection of the Deveta Transverzala and Safeta Hadzica Streets. The buses continued moving with the injured passengers and reached us in Dobrinja -- in fact, it reached Dobrinja where the injured received medical treatment. I went to the location where the bus was parked, and I photographed the physical evidence that I found on the bus and inside the bus. I drafted an official report and made a photo file.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, I'm going to show you your report in a moment. Just -- you said it was an Elektroprenos bus. Was that a military vehicle or a civilian vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was a civilian bus for civilian transport. A girl was killed on that occasion. There were civilians in the bus, and Elektroprenos is a company that existed before the war and in fact it still exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can't see this, but I don't think that it is contained in any of the counts of the indictment. I don't know what incident we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, my learned friend is correct. It's not an illustrative incident as in the ones that are appended to the indictment; it is, however, an unscheduled incident that the Prosecution submits it's entitled to lead evidence on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: 138 -- Witness 138, first of all, how did you come to know about this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the police station in Novi Grad, and I was informed about this incident by my boss, who had received a report from the scene itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you said you went to the incident -- sorry, you went to the location where the bus was parked and photographed the physical evidence. Where was that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus was parked in front of the infirmary in the Dobrinja neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And was that where the bus was hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The bus had been hit at the crossroads of the -- at the intersection of the Deveta Transverzala and Safeta Hadzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, I'm going to ask you to show that location in a moment on the map, but how did you establish that that was where the bus was hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the examination and the inspection of the bus and all the physical evidence there, we took photographs, I took photographs of the bus, and we learned from the eye-witnesses that that was where the bus was hit. After the inspection and photographing the bus, we went back to this location and we found evidence indicating that this was the place where the bus had been hit. We found broken glass there, so that was the location where the bus had been hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just concentrating on that location where you found broken glass, how did you know that the glass was -- indeed, glass from the bus and not from other vehicles or from other sources?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very busy intersection. Before that there had been no activities that would have resulted in any glass breaking. The broken glass had been recently broken at that time. The quantity of the broken glass also indicated that this was glass originating from the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How did you know that it was broken glass that had recently -- that was recently broken? How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of the glass fragments, you can draw conclusions whether the glass had been broken recently, immediately before the inspection, or whether it had been there for some time. Cars passing over it, dust, and so on, would have left traces on the broken glass, but this glass had no such traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So let me just see if I understand you. Are you saying that if the glass had dust traces on them, it would have been glass that had been there for some time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. At the location where this glass was, this broken glass was, it was shiny, glimmering, and this indicated to us that this was something that had happened recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, from your inspection of the bus, were you able to establish where the damage -- where on the bus was damaged -- damage sustained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus was hit on the right-hand side. The round hit the window, which is why there was so much glass. It was actually hit in a place between the first and the second windows. That would be the front right-hand side of the bus. It was hit at the place where the roof and the side of the bus meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. Court Deputy, could we have map 2872 brought up, please. And if it could be zoomed in, please. And maybe if it could be moved so that the left-hand side of the map is showing a little bit more. That's correct. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, are you able to see where the -- where the investigation concluded the bus was hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can indicate the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you indicate -- can you indicate that position with the letter B.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the intersection, and I will put letter B there. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Which direction was the bus travelling -- in which direction was the bus travelling at the time it was hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was moving along this road. It says here Ive Andrica, but this is in fact called Deveta Transverzala Street, and it was moving in the direction of Dobrinja, along this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just for clarity, is the street name Deveta Transverzala Street, is that a new or an old name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, only the beginning of this street is called Ive Andrica Street and this whole neighbourhood is divided into a number of what we called Transverzala sections, and this is the ninth such section, "Deveta Transverzala" in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you, with an arrow, draw a line in the direction in which the bus was travelling, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the only thing I'm interested in now - and I think the Prosecutor was supposed to do that - I don't even know, I didn't hear the date when this occurred. Could we please see whether this is in the period relevant for the indictment. Let us first determine that. What is the date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's basic and important.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I, of course, am leading evidence of an incident within the indictment period. I understand the concern of my friend. I intend to show the witness an investigation report that he produced, and that I submit will clarify the matter. I just want the witness to mark this incident on the map. I can do the document now. It's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, well, stick to the procedure you had planned to follow, and you'll get to the date shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, the line that you have drawn on the map, can you just -- just for clarity, which direction is that? Is that north to south? South to north? East to west? Can you tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the direction in which the bus was moving, from south to north, or rather, from north to south, along the Deveta Transverzala Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in order to be able to follow the examination-in-chief at all, I would have to know what the date is. I have to know that. I can't follow the examination-in-chief if I don't know the date. This is not cross-examination by the Prosecutor in which I can then sit here and wait for the Prosecution to come to that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have already ruled on this matter. The Prosecutor is going to get to the evidence which will disclose the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, can you also now mark the place where you saw the bus for the first time; in other words, where the bus had come to park.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map is zoomed in in such a way that I can't really show it, but I've put a dot here where Dobrinja is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's fine. Can you put the letter D there, please, where the dot is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you told the Trial Chamber just a moment ago that the damage was sustained on the right side of the bus. Did the location of the damage enable you to determine the direction in which the projectile came and hit the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the damage, it can be said that the projectile had come in from the right, which indicated to us the direction from which the round had been fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say "right," can you tell us in terms of west, east, north, south.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when the bus entered this intersection, it was hit from its right. That would be from the west, if you look at this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you draw a line indicating the direction of fire, please. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And can you put on top of the arrow the letter P.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, on that map are you able to locate the hill called Mojmilo hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It's here, the green area here, where it says "Novi Grad."

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you just please mark that with the letter M.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Given the fact that the bus sustained damage on the right-hand side -- on the right-hand side, would it have been possible for the shots to have come from Mojmilo hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In that case a bus would have sustained a direct hit from the driver's side or from the left side of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And when you examined the bus, did you see damage on the driver's side and the left-hand side of the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It had damage only the way that I described it a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'd like to offer this still into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P147, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And are we getting to the date now?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And before I ask for this 65 ter number to be brought up, might we go into private session, with your leave, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, I know it was a long time ago, but in the very beginning of my examination you told the Trial Chamber that you were involved in an investigation of sniping incidents. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember investigating sniping incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And again, very briefly, what was your role when it came to investigating sniping incidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon receiving a report on an injury or a killing, we would go to the scene. My duty was to examine the scene, to find physical evidence with respect to the action that had been taken, to photograph the scene, do the measurements, and based on the traces, to determine the direction of the firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does the name Jasmina Tabakovic mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with that name in connection with the on-site investigation that I was involved in in May 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you recall the exact day in May 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 15th of May, 1995, and I also wrote an official report, and it should bear an exact date. But I do think it was the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What happened on that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I carried out the on-site investigation on the 15th of May, and the incident happened on the 14th of May at 15 minutes before midnight. An investigation report -- an on-site investigation should typically be done on the following day because we were not equipped for doing night-time investigations. A bullet came through a window. There was no window-pane in this window but only a plastic sheet. The bullet penetrated the plastic sheet at a certain level that I recorded, and it hit Jasmina Tabakovic above her left breast. It went through her body and exited below her left shoulder blade. It hit the cupboard and got embedded in the wall. As a result of this hit, Jasmina Tabakovic died.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, you said a bullet came through the window. A window of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a window of the room where she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the room was part of -- was it part of an office? Was it part of a private house? Can you tell the Trial Chamber that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say "room," I don't mean office that was in the flat of Jasmina Tabakovic. It was in an apartment building in Dobrinja. She was in that flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, when you went to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When was this investigation carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was carried out on the 15th of May, and as I said, I cannot remember the exact date. But I do remember that it took place on the 14th of May, at 2345 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But in any event, would it have been the day after the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. We were able to conduct investigation in daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, were you able, on that occasion, to determine the direction in which the bullet came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on the traces, I could establish where the bullet had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say "traces," what traces do you speak about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means the penetration of the bullet through the plastic sheet, through the cupboard, and the bullet that we recovered from the wall behind this cupboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Were you able to establish a line from the damage in the plastic sheeting to the cupboard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure of recovering this kind of clues indicates that when you have a damage through the plastic sheet and the damage to the wall itself. So we took a piece of rope and connected these two points, and we were able to establish the exact trajectory of the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And in which direction was it concluded the bullet came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bullet came from Dobrinja 1, that means from apartment buildings in the Dobrinja neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Which party to the conflict controlled the area comprised -- comprising Dobrinja 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the area under the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you said that you found a bullet in the flat. From that bullet, were you able to establish the weapon that was used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That bullet was sent for expert examination, but at a glance it was obvious that it was a rifle bullet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Prosecutor, could you ask the witness if he can inform us of the calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 138, are you able to tell the Court the calibre of the weapon that was used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report I said that it was 7.62-millimetre rifle bullet, but the proper procedure was that I was bound to send this slug for expert examination. These were just -- this was just initial information that I provided for further investigation by inspectors. However, my statement could have been disputed by an expert witness who inspected this slug in the laboratory of the CSB. But in agreement with our -- my superiors, I was allowed, in this brief description, to specify the calibre, although further analysis was able to dispute or confirm my claims. As far as -- according to my knowledge at that time, I was able to say that this was a 7.62-millimetre ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I wanted to ask you about, lastly, another sniping incident that you investigated. Do you remember an incident on the 3rd of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this incident. It happened in an apartment building on Emile Zola Street, in the Dobrinja neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Briefly tell the Trial Chamber what happened in that incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon receiving a report about the incident, I went to the scene, and my supervisor told me that in the ground floor flat on Emile Zola Street, a woman had been hit. I believe that her name was Semka Kozadra.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you produce a report from your investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I photographed the scene and recovered the physical evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to move into private session, with your leave, to bring up the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You said that a bullet was found in the corridor. Are you able to establish -- were you able to establish the weapon from which it came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that the casing was found but the bullet was found on the floor of the corridor, and it was a 7.62-millimetre rifle bullet, which was also sent for forensic examination to be verified by an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Was the woman who was hit, did she -- was she killed or was she injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she was wounded. And before the on-site investigation team arrived, she had been transferred to the Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And in this investigation, were you able to establish the direction from where the bullet came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Based on the penetration of the blanket, which served as a visual shield, how it passed through the room, how it passed through the plastic sheet and the door of the room, we were able to reconstruct the trajectory. And we did it in the same way by stretching a piece of rope, and thereby establishing the direction from which the bullet had come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask you, then, what was there about the plastic sheet and the door that enabled you to determine the direction from which the bullet came? What was there about the passage of the bullet through the plastic sheet and the door that enabled you to determine the direction from which it came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hole in the plastic sheet and the hole in the blanket, the hole in the window and the door, so all these holes indicated where the bullet had passed through. At this time all the glass was virtually broken and people used plastic sheets provided by the humanitarian organisations in order to cover the windows. So when a bullet passes through a plastic sheet on the window it leaves a hole behind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but I still have to press you further as to what was there about the hole. What was so specific about the hole that enabled you to make this determination? I mean a hole is a hole.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When a bullet passes through a plastic sheet, on either side the sheet is penetrated and it breaks on the side from which the bullet came, and it showed that the hole and the size of the hole showed that -- and indicated that it was caused by this particular bullet. There were no other damage on the sheet, and it confirmed that the bullet passed through. Maybe it's difficult to explain now, but when you see it with the naked eye, I knew precisely that this hole was caused by the passage of a bullet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, continue. We just have -- we have a couple minutes now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. This is the last document I'm going to show the witness, and then I'm done. Can we move into private session for this last document, please, because it's -- with your leave, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 1st day of February, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25
